2609.18688.title: Generalist-Specialist Mixture-of-Experts for Rare Pathology Detection in Multimodal Imaging
2609.18688.paper_summary: AI models for multimodal medical imaging must balance modality-specific specialization with cross-modal shared representations, a trade-off that pure Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures currently fail to satisfy. Expert-based routing improves in-domain learning but may sacrifice cross-modal signals, which appear particularly important for rare (low-prevalence) pathologies in our experiments. To resolve this, we introduce Generalist-Specialist-MoE (GS-MoE), a two-branch (MoE) architecture that couples a cross-modal generalist model with distinct modality-specific specialists (experts) via domain-constrained feature fusion. On RadImageNet (1.35M images, 165 pathologies, three modalities), GS-MoE recovers detection of six low-prevalence pathologies on which every baseline scores F1 $=$ 0, with per-class gains up to +0.60 F1. It attains this while even slightly exceeding dense and specialist-only MoE aggregate baselines (MCC 0.770), while using ${\sim}53\%$ fewer active parameters at inference than the strongest investigated dense model.
2609.18688.paper_summary_zh: AI 模型在多模態醫學影像中必須在特定模態的專業化與跨模態的共享表徵之間取得平衡，這是一個純粹的專家混合（MoE）架構目前無法滿足的權衡。基於專家的路由改善了領域內的學習，但可能會犧牲跨模態信號，而這在我們的實驗中對於罕見（低流行率）病理顯得尤其重要。為了解決這個問題，我們引入了通才-專家-MoE（GS-MoE），這是一種雙分支（MoE）架構，通過領域約束的特徵融合將跨模態的通才模型與不同的模態專家（專家）相結合。在 RadImageNet（1.35M 圖像，165 種病理，三種模態）上，GS-MoE 恢復了六種低流行率病理的檢測，這些病理在每個基準上得分 F1 $=$ 0，並且每類的增益高達 +0.60 F1。它在這一過程中甚至略微超越了密集和專家專用 MoE 的總體基準（MCC 0.770），同時在推理時使用的主動參數比調查過的最強密集模型少了 ${\sim}53\%$。
